example.detection_method: Email gateway with advanced attachment scanning identified embedded VBA macros. Network IDS detected HTTP GET requests from internal hosts to an unusual external IP (198.51.100.55). Correlation with domain registration dates revealed suspiciously young sender domain. Endpoint monitoring flagged Office processes creating unusual HTTP requests shortly after document open.

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a spear phishing attack scenario targeting a specific high-value individual (CFO) within an organization, aligning well with the problem nature. The use of a malicious Excel attachment with embedded macros to exfiltrate credentials is a realistic and common tactic in spear phishing campaigns. All required fields are present and populated with detailed, plausible technical data including email headers, SMTP logs, macro code, domain registration info, and indicators that clearly support the identification of the attack. The indicators section effectively highlights key evidence such as the suspicious attachment, macro presence, domain age, and network activity, which together justify the classification as spear phishing. The detection method description is comprehensive and demonstrates practical risk reduction measures like advanced email scanning, network IDS, and endpoint monitoring. The inclusion of relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques further strengthens the sample's completeness and applicability. Overall, this sample is well-constructed, realistic, and thorough, making it a valid representation of the stated cybersecurity problem.

example.detection_method: Email gateway SPF failure alerts flagged spoofed domain. URL reputation services identified micros0ft-support.com as a homograph phishing domain. Web proxy logs showed POST requests containing credential parameters to suspicious domain. User reports and endpoint telemetry confirmed access attempts to the phishing site.

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a spear phishing attack targeting a specific role (HR manager) within an organization, aligning well with the problem nature. The use of a homograph domain (micros0ft-support.com) to mimic a legitimate Microsoft Teams support domain is a realistic and common tactic in spear phishing. The technical data is comprehensive, including email headers showing SPF failure, SMTP transaction logs, domain registration details indicating a recently created suspicious domain, URL analysis highlighting confusable characters, web server logs showing credential capture activity, and a snippet of captured credentials. Indicators clearly explain why this is a spear phishing example, such as SPF failure, domain age, confusable domain, and unusual POST requests. The detection method description ties together multiple detection points, including email gateway alerts, URL reputation services, web proxy logs, and user reports, demonstrating a multi-layered detection approach. Relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are correctly identified, covering phishing, credential access, and infrastructure. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and well-documented, effectively illustrating the stated cybersecurity problem and risk reduction context.
